paragraphs.title: A Call to Awaken and Repent

answers: O nation not desired
The shepherds
The Philistines
easy.explanation: Verse 1 calls the nation not desired to gather together.
easy.q: Whom does the prophet tell to gather together?

answers: A great harvest
The fierce anger of the LORD
The restoration of Judah
easy.explanation: Verse 2 warns that the fierce anger of the LORD may come upon them.
easy.q: What may come before the people act?

answers: Wealth and honor
Cities and fortresses
The LORD, righteousness, and meekness
easy.explanation: Verse 3 tells them to seek the LORD, righteousness, and meekness.
easy.q: What are the people told to seek?

answers: The day of the LORD’s anger may soon come
The cities have already become pastureland
The nations have already worshipped the LORD
medium.explanation: The repeated word “before” warns them to act before the day of the LORD’s anger arrives.
medium.q: Why must the people act quickly according to verses 1–2?

answers: Gentle kindness
Intense anger
A place of shelter
medium.explanation: “Fierce” describes anger that is strong and intense.
medium.q: In the phrase “the fierce anger of the LORD,” what does “fierce” describe?

answers: Those who seek Him may be hidden in the day of His anger
Those who seek Him will rule Philistia
Those who seek Him will rebuild the cities
medium.explanation: The verse says that those who seek the LORD, righteousness, and meekness may be hidden in that day.
medium.q: What connection does verse 3 make between seeking the LORD and shelter?

answers: That judgment has already ended
That action may be delayed
That the time to repent is limited
challenge.explanation: The repeated warning shows that the people must act before the approaching day of judgment.
challenge.q: What does the repetition of “before” in verse 2 emphasize?

answers: Meekness
Pride
Riches
challenge.q: Which quality is added to seeking the LORD and righteousness?

answers: Shelter is guaranteed to everyone
Shelter is possible but not stated as an absolute guarantee
There is no connection between conduct and shelter
challenge.explanation: The phrase “it may be” expresses possibility rather than an unconditional promise.
challenge.q: What does “it may be” suggest at the end of verse 3?

paragraphs.title: The Destruction of Philistia and the Restoration of Judah

answers: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, and Ekron
Nineveh, Assyria, and Moab
Jerusalem, Bethel, and Hebron
easy.explanation: Verse 4 names Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, and Ekron.
easy.q: Which cities are named as being forsaken, made desolate, driven out, or rooted up?

answers: A royal palace
Dwellings and cottages for shepherds, and folds for flocks
A battlefield only
easy.explanation: Verse 6 says the sea coast will become dwellings and cottages for shepherds and folds for flocks.
easy.q: What will the sea coast become?

answers: The remnant of the house of Judah
The children of Ammon
The kings of Assyria
easy.explanation: Verse 7 says the coast will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah.
easy.q: Who will possess the coast and lie down in the houses of Ashkelon?

answers: The cities are destroyed, the region becomes pastureland, and Judah returns
Judah is destroyed, the Philistines return, and the sea dries up
The nations worship, Nineveh is rebuilt, and the cities are filled
medium.explanation: The passage moves from the destruction of Philistine cities to pastureland and then to the return of Judah’s remnant.
medium.q: What sequence of events is described in verses 4–7?

answers: A deserted and ruined place
A place filled with people
A place with abundant water
medium.explanation: A desolation is a ruined or abandoned place.
medium.q: What does “a desolation” mean in the description of Ashkelon?

answers: The ruined region becomes a place where the remnant can pasture and dwell
Judah’s remnant destroys the cities of Judah
Judah’s remnant moves into the land of Moab
medium.explanation: Verse 7 describes the remnant feeding there and lying down in the houses of Ashkelon.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the ruined cities and Judah’s remnant?

answers: The passage moves from the destruction of Philistia to the return and rest of Judah’s remnant
The passage moves from war between Judah and Egypt to peace between Assyria and Moab
The passage moves from building cities to destroying the temple
challenge.explanation: The first verses describe devastation, while verse 7 describes Judah’s restoration and rest.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears between verses 4–6 and verse 7?

answers: The remnant will find rest and security in the land
The remnant will immediately leave the land
The remnant will wage war at night
challenge.explanation: Lying down in the evening suggests peaceful rest and settlement.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the remnant lying down in the evening?

answers: The remnant of the house of Judah
The LORD their God
The shepherds of Philistia
challenge.explanation: Verse 7 says, “the LORD their God shall visit them, and turn away their captivity.”
challenge.q: Who is said to turn away the captivity of Judah?

paragraphs.title: Judgment on Moab and Ammon and the End of Their Pride

answers: For reproaching the LORD’s people and magnifying themselves
For building coastal cities
For feeding flocks
easy.explanation: Verse 8 mentions their reproach and their proud actions against the LORD’s people.
easy.q: Why are Moab and the children of Ammon judged?

answers: A flourishing garden
Sodom and Gomorrah
Great Nineveh
easy.explanation: Verse 9 compares Moab to Sodom and the children of Ammon to Gomorrah.
easy.q: To what will Moab and Ammon be compared?

answers: Worship the LORD
Rebuild Moab’s cities
Hide from Judah
easy.explanation: Verse 11 says that all the isles of the heathen shall worship Him.
easy.q: What will the isles of the heathen do according to verse 11?

answers: Their punishment is presented as the consequence of their reproach and pride
Their pride protects their land
Their pride causes them to return to Judah
medium.explanation: Verse 10 says their desolation will be the result of their pride and reproach.
medium.q: How is the pride of Moab and Ammon related to their punishment?

answers: Words of praise
Abusive or insulting words
Songs of victory
medium.explanation: Revilings are harsh insults or words of abuse.
medium.q: What does “revilings” mean in the phrase “the revilings of the children of Ammon”?

answers: It removes their power and sense of superiority
It strengthens their rule
It enables them to conquer Judah
medium.explanation: Their desolation is portrayed as the judgment that ends their proud self-exaltation.
medium.q: How does the destruction of Moab and Ammon affect their pride?

answers: Moab and Ammon are humbled, while other peoples recognize the LORD’s power
Moab and Ammon rule over all other nations
All nations stop worshipping the LORD
challenge.explanation: The proud nations are judged, while people from the isles of the heathen worship the LORD.
challenge.q: What change in the nations’ status is described in verses 10–11?

answers: The remnant will take possession of these lands after their judgment
Moab and Ammon will conquer the remnant
The remnant will disappear from the land
challenge.explanation: Verse 9 says the residue and remnant of the LORD’s people shall spoil and possess them.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the statement that the residue of the LORD’s people shall spoil Moab and Ammon?

answers: A solemn declaration that strengthens the certainty of God’s word
A description of the lives of Moab’s kings
An invitation to a celebration
challenge.explanation: The phrase introduces a solemn divine declaration and emphasizes the certainty of the judgment.
challenge.q: What does the opening phrase “As I live, saith the LORD” communicate?

paragraphs.title: Punishment from the South to the North

answers: The Ethiopians
The shepherds of Judah
The children of Ammon
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says, “Ye Ethiopians also, ye shall be slain by my sword.”
easy.q: Who is mentioned at the beginning of this section as being slain?

answers: Assyria and Nineveh
Moab and Gaza
Ammon and Ashkelon
easy.explanation: Verse 13 says that the LORD will destroy Assyria and make Nineveh a desolation.
easy.q: Which kingdom and city will the LORD destroy in the north?

answers: A center of commerce
A desolation, dry like a wilderness
Dwellings for shepherds only
easy.explanation: Verse 13 describes Nineveh as a desolation, dry like a wilderness.

answers: From the south toward the north
From the north toward the south only
From the sea toward the wilderness only
medium.explanation: The passage first mentions the Ethiopians and then moves northward to Assyria and Nineveh.
medium.q: What general direction does the judgment cover in this section?

answers: It will be dry and desolate
It will be crowded with people
It will become a green pasture
medium.explanation: The comparison describes a barren and abandoned place.
medium.q: What does “dry like a wilderness” communicate about Nineveh?

answers: A secure and proud city will become a deserted place inhabited by animals and birds
A ruined city will become even greater
A small village will become Judah’s capital
medium.explanation: Verses 14–15 contrast Nineveh’s former confidence and rejoicing with its future desolation and animal inhabitants.
medium.q: What change will take place in Nineveh?

answers: The city has lost its human inhabitants and become desolate
The city has grown stronger militarily
The city has been filled with merchants
challenge.explanation: Animals occupying the city’s buildings show that its people are gone and it has become desolate.
challenge.q: What does the presence of flocks and birds inside Nineveh show?

answers: A city saying, “I am, and there is none beside me,” becomes a place for beasts to lie down
A poor city is contrasted with a wealthy city
An agricultural city is contrasted with a shepherd city
challenge.explanation: Nineveh’s proud self-confidence is contrasted with its humiliating ruin.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in the description of Nineveh?

answers: The dramatic change between Nineveh’s former condition and its ruined state
The happiness of Nineveh’s inhabitants
The success of the city’s construction
challenge.explanation: The question highlights the sharp reversal from a rejoicing, careless city to a desolate place.
challenge.q: What does the question “How is she become a desolation?” emphasize?
